hits.title: Realtime Robotics Names Kevin Carlin Chief Executive Officer to Lead Company’s Next Phase of Growth - Realtime Robotics
hits.snippet: Realtime Robotics names Kevin Carlin CEO to lead its next growth phase, with co-founder Peter Howard continuing as Chairman of the Board. BOSTON – August 13, 2026 – Realtime Robotics, the leader in industrial AI for automated robot system design and deployment, today announced that Kevin Carlin has been appointed Chief Executive Officer, effective immediately. Carlin brings more than two decades of international leadership in semiconductors, industrial automation, and AI to the role. He joined Realtime Robotics in 2022 as Chief Commercial Officer and was promoted to President and Chief Commercial Officer in 2025. Prior to Realtime Robotics, Carlin spent more than 13 years at Analog Devices, where he most recently built an internal startup focused on AI- and machine learning-driven sensing and analytics. Realtime Robotics’ Resolver platform automates and optimizes the most complex aspects of factory planning and robot system design and deployment. About Realtime Robotics Realtime Robotics is the leader in industrial AI for automated robot system design and deployment.

Realtime Robotics has appointed Kevin Carlin as Chief Executive Officer as the industrial AI company moves into its next phase of commercial growth and expands adoption of its Resolver platform among major automotive manufacturers.
The leadership transition comes as Realtime Robotics reports growing adoption of Resolver among global automotive OEMs seeking to use AI to streamline factory planning, shorten vehicle development timelines, manage increasingly complex production environments, and accelerate the deployment of robotic manufacturing systems.
Realtime Robotics has also expanded its workforce while continuing to develop Resolver’s capabilities, positioning the company to scale its commercial operations as more manufacturers incorporate AI into production planning and automation.
The company also sees opportunities to expand beyond automotive manufacturing over time. Realtime Robotics believes many of the challenges addressed by Resolver, including complex factory planning, robotic system design, engineering bottlenecks, and production changes, are also present in other sophisticated manufacturing sectors.
